tool.title: Journeys viewer
tool.description: Draw every journey (`user-scenario`) and workshop (`workshop`) in the checkout as static pages at the route of the visualiser an instance declares for this Tool, `<locale>/<instance>/<id>/`: an index of all journeys, grouped by instance (each a sub-graph page) and by `partOf`, ordered along `follows`; one page per journey, a journey map with a lane and a feeling curve per persona, then each step with its BPMN drawing (the step's flow nodes highlighted), user stories, requirements, FHIR examples, building blocks and ArchiMate views; and the workshop layer, the questions for the room on each step, a page per workshop and per module, job aids, and printable A3/A4 sheets. Instances below the declaring one are read through their declarations, so a downstream site shows the journeys of the layers it mounts too.

inputs.name: instance
inputs.description: The instance whose `visualisers` declare this Tool: the pages go to that visualiser's route. One that declares none gets nothing, and the run exits 78 (not applicable).

inputs.name: site
inputs.description: A site being built: the pages are written at the declared route under it. Absent, under the instance's own site directory. The route is this Tool's alone and is replaced whole.

outputs.name: pages
outputs.description: The viewer's pages and its two assets (`assets/journeys.css`, `assets/journeys.js`), under the declared route.

selection.when: A site build of an instance that declares a `journeys-viewer` visualiser over its `user-scenario` and `workshop` directories; run with the other declared writers (`visualiser-writers.ts`), before the navbar pass.
selection.limits: Static pages: the stepper, the filter and the remembered assessment ticks are a small dependency-free script, and every page reads complete without it. A FHIR example links to its page only where an instance declares a `fhir-artifact-index`; an ArchiMate view is drawn only where its instance declares `archimate-pages`.
selection.cost: Milliseconds per journey; a BPMN drawing is inlined once per step that names it.

$comment.comment: Owner, 2026-11-05 (option A): a generic journey and workshop viewer in the harness, so that a demonstrator's journeys and an IG's pilgrim journey are content instances of it rather than apps of their own.
